result:
I've written the DG7 gate record as **BLOCKED**. The product and the reviews pass the audit, but the gate validator fails on four defects in the delivery records.

My first draft of the gate was APPROVED. Writing it let `validate.mjs --stage DG7` run its full checks for the first time. Without a gate record the validator stops at "file not found (gates/DG7.json)". That is why the earlier rounds, the round-7 reviewers and my own first run saw nothing else. With the record present it reported 120 problems, and only one concerns my in-flight run. Under the assignment's rule, that means BLOCKED.

**New findings: F-DG7-996 to F-DG7-999.** All are Medium and mandatory, owned by delivery-orchestrator. They have no product effect.

| Finding | Problem | Validator errors | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-DG7-996 | Leftover runner scratch files under `runs/DG7` were committed by concurrent commits and later deleted or changed in six commits (f6686f0d7, b4f501c3f, 3b72c507f, 8d0abc3f9, 12229e6b6, cabf14268). The final run records are intact. | 57 write-once errors | Already in git history; needs your decision (a clean re-gate as in D-238, or a reviewed change to the gate rules) |
| F-DG7-997 | `stages.json` review rounds 7, 8 and 9 say frozen at 18:39:59Z; the manifest says 18:39:12Z | 3 | Correct `stages.json`; no re-freeze needed |
| F-DG7-998 | For 19 closed findings, `findings.json` copies qa-verifier's verification, but the validator picks code-security-reviewer's (domain-reviewer's for 971). Every reviewer's verification in those rounds is PASS by a non-owner, so the closures themselves are valid. | 57 | Re-import with `import-findings.mjs`; no re-freeze needed |
| F-DG7-999 | `stages.json` round 5 lists a `qa-verifier.json` that the killed run never wrote | 2 | Correct `stages.json`; no re-freeze needed |

**Everything else holds:**
- **Candidate:** `sha256:0d71d445…2272` (3158 files) recomputes to the recorded value. Only metadata records changed after the freeze. DG0–DG6 historical validation and `--pipeline` pass.
- **Reviews:** the three round-7 PASS records come from three separate, successful, sandboxed runs. Each is a full review, not just of the last change. No reviewer implemented DG7 work.
- **Findings:** all 22 earlier closures hold, with valid fix commits. F-DG7-973 stays accepted as an observation. I re-judged that acceptance and concur.
- **Pre-freeze checks:** 17 of 19 passed. The 2 failures came from two allow-list entries that were stale in the payload scope; once those were scoped to history, both checks re-ran green. Live CI was not run and is recorded as a disclosed residual.
- **Evidence:** every failure line in the reviewers' cited logs is disclosed and explained. Spot-checked screenshots and drill reports match the claims.
- **Requirements:** 54/54 rows are IMPLEMENTED and the register check passes. The exceptions are REQ-DLV-014 and REQ-DLV-005, whose gate-time clauses need `validate --stage DG7` to pass.
- **Disclosures I had to decide:** the DG7 protocol hits (assignments missing elements, handbacks missing a section, the late DG6 historical log) and the partial A27 K11 drill result do not block on their own. I also accept the D-274 extension. They are form defects in records that can't be rewritten, with no product effect, and the substance behind them checks out.
- **Gate separation:** nothing grants a business approval or claims certification, and product G6 is never tied to DG7.

**Final `node tools/gates/validate.mjs --stage DG7`: exit 1, 145 problems.**
- 1 is my in-flight run: "invocation: file not found (`docs/delivery/runs/DG7/DG7-T-DG7-AUDIT-R9-release-auditor-20261116T211135Z-d27cb0e9/meta.json`)".
- 119 are the four defects above.
- 25 follow from this BLOCKED outcome:
  - "decision is BLOCKED" and the blocking conditions;
  - my FAIL verdict, checks and gate tests;
  - F-DG7-996 to 999 not yet imported into `findings.json`.

**Observations, not findings:**
- The protocol audit's count of incomplete assignments is now 29, and will be 30 once this run's record exists, against the 27 disclosed. The extra three are the round-8 and round-9 assignments, which the tool flags only because its keyword patterns miss elements that are present in the text. The sealing report should say so.
- ADR-0071 still needs its dated amendment (F-DG7-973 follow-up, owner solution-architect).
- The gate validator should run its record checks even when the gate record is missing.

After the four defects are fixed and imported, a new release audit has to run `validate --stage DG7` with a gate record present.

Files are in `docs/delivery/`:
- `gates/DG7.json`
- `reviews/DG7/round-9/release-auditor.json`
- `reviews/DG7/round-9/release-auditor.findings.json`
- `test-evidence/DG7/audit/round-9/` (29 logs)
